_frame_plan_note: Six shots on the proven 32.0s/960-frame shape. Each shot's narration_en is the sentence spoken over it; must_show_while_spoken lists the physical conditions that have to be true in the simulated state AND visible in the picture for at least min_seconds while that sentence is spoken.
_edit_order_note: Shot order follows retention evidence from an earlier episode (steepest viewer loss at 3.5-6 s when the picture went from an event to an explanation; second loss at a closing summary): action continues after the hook, the diagram comes third, and the ending loops back to the first frame. Whether that pattern transfers to this episode is unverified.
test_conditions: Simulation. Two 1,500 kg cars at 90 km/h, head-on, no braking. Fixed post: assumed 0.8 m deceleration distance. Breakaway post: plastic impulse at bumper height plus an assumed 250 N s to shear the slip base.

shots.visual_proof: Two identical cars (blue in the fixed-post lane, red in the breakaway lane) hit two identical-looking sign posts at the same instant, slow motion 0.12x: seen from ahead, then from the side as the freed post turns over the red car, then from behind with the blue car stopped at its post. Speed read-outs for both cars come from the simulation.
shots.narration_en: Two cars hit the same steel sign post at the same speed but only one of them stops.

shots.visual_proof: Extreme slow motion (0.008x) at the foot of the breakaway post: the bumper arrives, the upper plate slides off the lower plate, the three bolts are thrown clear and the foot of the post is carried forward.
shots.narration_en: The second post was built to let go because its base slips apart the instant the bumper hits.

shots.visual_proof: Exploded view (diagram device): the post is lifted off its base and set back so the two plates and the three bolts between them can be seen. No car in this shot.
shots.narration_en: Its two plates are held by bolts in open notches that resist the wind but not a moving car.

shots.visual_proof: Side view at 0.14x: struck low, the freed post turns foot-first up and over the red car and comes down behind it. Translucent copies of the post every 0.06 s (stroboscopic marks, a diagram device) trace the arc.
shots.narration_en: Hit low, the freed post spins up and over the roof and lands on the road behind the car.

shots.visual_proof: Both lanes again at 0.12x from behind and then from the side: the blue car's read-out falls to 0 within the assumed 0.8 m deceleration distance of a fixed post; the red car's read-out barely moves.
shots.narration_en: The fixed post took all of the car's speed in under a meter while the breakaway post took almost none.

shots.visual_proof: Three signs on slip bases along a roadside while a car passes; the last two seconds return to the opening camera with both cars arriving at the posts again, ending one frame before the film's first frame so the Short loops.
shots.narration_en: So the signs along fast roads stand on bases like this, waiting to let go.

first_three_seconds.note: Counts physical events becoming true and visible, not cuts or camera moves.
